f128.summary: The Duke of Sessa, imperial ambassador in Rome, to Charles V (DECODE's '1424' is a typo): the bishop of Veroli's report from Constance on the Swiss diet and cantons arming for France; in cipher, that the Pope's secretary Felice would not show the bishop's own letters, that the report agrees with what the bishop wrote to the postmaster, and that Sessa asked the Pope for a provision for the Swiss business, having opened the peace-and-truce negotiation. Key rebuilt from the sibling letters' contemporary decipherments.
f128.en:
Having written and closed the packet of the duplicate of the 14th of this month, which will come with this, I saw a
letter of the Bishop Verulano, who is at Constance, of which I send a copy herewith. I then sent to His Holiness to beg
him to have me told of any particular, so as to give notice of it where fitting. He sent me Felice, his secretary, who
has told me that the letters he has are from the said Verulano, of the 6th and 7th of this month, where he says that
the diet was over, and that Lucerne did not conclude to give help to the French;

r9873.summary: Sessa to Charles V, a holograph with cipher runs and a postscript wholly in cipher; no decipherment is bound with it (Bergenroth's CSP Spain ii 637 calendars Goicoechea's 19th-century reading, and nos. 636/638 the triplicate and the court abstract, used only as a topic crib). Transcribed in full; each line (a) cipher, (b) reading.
r9873.en:
Where it was needed I have said what Your Majesty commands me about the disbanding of the army in those parts.

[clear text not transcribed]

It was already known through France, though with some additions, because they want to make out that Your Majesty
was holding cortes in Burgos and would then hold them in Aragon and Catalonia, and with the [?grant] that […sig]s
[?it is known] he was coming to [?Italy], which does not please all the ears of this court.

The [?coming] of the Archbishop of Capua will settle these disturbances; it is known today that he left Blois on the
seventh of this month with the articles of truce that he had indicated there, of which His Holiness has ordered a copy
to be given to me.

[?Before] […sas]ission from here, I proposed two things:

r9898.summary: Sessa to Charles V, written on the day of Pavia, before the news: Italy, the Pope and the datary's attempt to bring the Duke over to the French; six runs carry a marginal decipherment of the time, the rest is read here with the key. Not calendared in CSP iii.1.

bne52-7.summary: Sessa reports the Pope's words: Italy confused since the viceroy left; the Pope pressed to join a league that England wants, which he has not and will not consent to; news by way of Bourbon; the French suspicious and fearful; the bishop of Bayeux now an avowed French ambassador; Casale to England; Alberto Pio back from Viterbo; the confirmation of the league; Pescara takes Saluzzo, the army unpaid.
bne52-7.en:
The last letter I wrote to Your Majesty is of the 14th of this month, by a courier who I heard was being dispatched
from Naples, with whom I sent the duplicate of the 12th; and with this goes the duplicate of that one.

As to the troops which ‹rob›…, what the Pope answered me is certain, because someone published it on purpose.

What His Holiness has told me to write to Your Majesty is that everything in Italy is confused and everyone in the
greatest suspicion, which has arisen from the departure of the viceroy without leaving matters here settled; and that
His Holiness has been, and always is, much required and pressed by many to make a league, and in England they desire
it and are dying for new negotiations;

system: Mixed nomenclator: three-letter code groups for words, names and syllables plus single letters and signs for spelling, with a clear/cipher switch sign and a null paragraph opener.
